title: Why Does Your Controller Shake?
description:
Why does your controller shake when you crash in a game? Inside each handle sits a tiny motor with a weight that's heavier on one side. When the motor spins, that lopsided weight yanks the controller back and forth dozens of times a second, and you feel it as rumble. The game decides how fast it spins.

On many controllers the left weight is heavy, for deep rumbles, and the right one is light, for quick buzzes. Newer controllers also use magnet coils for tiny, precise taps.
